bibliographic.title: Magnetic excitations in the quasi-2D ferromagnet Fe3 − xGeTe2 measured with inelastic neutron scattering

affiliations.text: Neutron Scattering Division, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Tennessee 37831, USA.
Materials Science and Technology Division, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Tennessee 37831, USA

bibliographic.abstract: Fe3 − xGeTe2 is an itinerant ferromagnet composed of two-dimensional layers weakly connected by van der Waals bonding that shows a variety of intriguing phenomena. Inelastic neutron scattering measurements on bulk single crystals of Fe2 . 75GeTe2 were performed to quantify the magnetic exchange interaction energies and anisotropy. The observed inelastic excitations are indicative of dominant in-plane correlations with negligible magnetic interactions between the layers. A spin-gap of 3.9 meV is observed allowing a measure of the magnetic anisotropy. As the excitations disperse to their maximum energy ( ∼ 65 meV) they become highly damped, reflective of both the magnetic site occupancy reduction of 25% on one Fe sublattice and the itinerant interactions. A minimal model is employed to describe the excitation spectra and extract nearest neighbor magnetic exchange interaction values. The temperature evolution of the excitations are probed and correlations shown to persist above Tc, indicative of low dimensional magnetism.

funding.funder: U. S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Basic Energy Sciences, Materials Sciences and Engineering Division

samples.sample_description: Bulk single crystals with 25% Fe(2) vacancies.

datasets.dataset_description: Measurements focused on the full energy range of the spectrum with incident energies of 120 meV and 50 meV at 10 K.
Measurements to resolve low energy scattering, spin-gap energy, and temperature dependence at 10 K, 160 K and 295 K with incident energies of 10 meV and 30 meV.
Measurement of an empty sample holder under the same conditions as the sample for background subtraction.
